# UMR-CPA phase state

`eos.umr_cpa_phase`

## Source

**Voutsas, E. et al. (2004)**

The Peng-Robinson cubic mixed by the UMR universal rule over UNIFAC-UMR-PRU activity coefficients, with the Wertheim association contribution added to the residual Helmholtz energy.

DOI: [10.1021/ie049580s](https://doi.org/10.1021/ie049580s)


## What this model is

A **direct** model: a computation over vectors, with no iteration and therefore no algorithm block. It is here because a calculation's inputs are scalars, so a composition vector has nowhere in the calc registry to go - and it is a model rather than a library function so that it goes through the spec-driven pipeline like everything else.

## Inputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `components` | - | the substances the mixture is made of, by name, resolved against the component databank with the UMR-CPA parameter set, the `UMRCPA_MC1..5` coefficients and the `UNIFACcompUMRPRU` group decomposition |
| `T` | K | absolute temperature |
| `P` | Pa | absolute pressure |
| `z` | dimensionless | the mixture's mole fractions, checked rather than renormalised |
| `compressed_phase` | liquid / vapour | which root describes the phase wanted. Not a compressibility factor: the association moves the root, so a caller could not supply one without solving the model first. |


## Outputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `z_factor` | dimensionless | the compressibility factor at the chosen root |
| `ln_phi` | dimensionless | the fugacity coefficients, as logarithms, at the chosen root |
| `h_res` | J/mol | the residual enthalpy, real minus ideal gas at the same temperature, pressure and composition, including the association's `-T d(A/RT)/dT` |
| `s_res` | J/(mol*K) | the residual entropy, real minus ideal gas at the same temperature, pressure and composition |

| Bound | On violation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `T > 0` | raises | an absolute temperature; zero and below are not states |
| `P > 0` | raises | an absolute pressure; zero and below are not states |

## Assumptions

- **the attraction is mixed by a universal rule, not by an interaction matrix.** `alpha_mix = sum_i x_i (a_i^T/(b_i R T) + hwfc ln gamma_i)` with `hwfc = -1/0.53`, and `A = n B R T alpha_mix` with the co-volume at the linear sum. No `kij` column is read.
- the `ln gamma_i` are UNIFAC-UMR-PRU's on the `_umrmc` tables, which is what `SystemUMRCPAEoS` pairs the rule with; that model's combinatorial term is Flory-Huggins, not plain UNIFAC's.
- `a` and `b` are the `UMRCPA_a0`/`UMRCPA_b` columns for a component that carries them - a third fitted set beside the SRK and PR families - and the bounding volume and energy are `UMRCPA_assocVolume`/`UMRCPA_assocEnergy`. Water's `kappa_AB` is 0.125 here against the PR family's.
- the attractive term is the five-parameter Mathias-Copeman form seeded with `UMRCPA_MC1..5`. A component without that set is **refused**, because NeqSim's per-component fallback is not expressible as one mixture-level alpha.
- the association is Wertheim first-order perturbation theory with a Carnahan-Starling radial distribution function: site schemes whose sites bond on a charge-sign product, an Elliott cross rule, and a successive-substitution site-fraction solve refined by Newton.
- **the root is not the cubic's.** The association carries a pressure, so the volume solves `f(Z) = Z - Z/(Z-B) + A Z/((Z+d1 B)(Z+d2 B)) - P_a Z/P = 0` with `P_a = -R T d(A_assoc/(R T))/dV`.
- no `cp_res`, because the association's second temperature derivative is not derived; it is absent from the outputs rather than reported from the cubic alone.
- **there is no flash.** `eos.pt_flash`'s Jacobian is `d ln phi / d n`, which every excess-Gibbs rule refuses because that derivative is the excess Gibbs energy's own Hessian.
